passage:
Monday. Sarita from the flat below stood in the corridor and shouted that Vijay's plant pots were dripping onto her laundry. A few doors opened a crack. Vijay's temper rose and the reply was hot on the tongue, but Vijay took a breath and said, "I can hear that this has upset you. Can we look at it tomorrow evening, just the two of us?"

Tuesday. They met at the balcony. Vijay saw a cracked saucer under one pot and offered to bring the pots inside and put trays under the rest. Sarita's voice dropped. "Fine. And I should not have shouted like that."

A week later. There were no more complaints. Sarita left a bag of curry leaves at Vijay's door.

qa.q: What was dripping onto Sarita's laundry?
qa.a: Water from Vijay's plant pots was dripping onto it.

qa.q: How can you tell that Vijay was angry but kept it in check?
qa.a: Vijay's temper rose and the reply was hot on the tongue, yet Vijay took a breath and offered to talk the next evening.

qa.q: What fix did Vijay offer for the dripping?
qa.a: To bring the pots inside and put trays under the rest.

qa.q: How did Sarita seem to feel by the end?
qa.a: Calmer and a little sorry, since she apologised for shouting and later left curry leaves.

grounding: A neighbour shouts over a small matter; the protagonist stays calm, offers to settle it privately later and avoids an audience.

passage:
Building manager's log, Palm Grove Apartments, Saturday 6 p.m.
Called to the courtyard by the guard. Gopika from 5C was shouting at Tanvir from 4C about water dripping from his balcony plants onto her washing. A few residents had come out to watch.
I saw Tanvir's hands close into fists, then open again. He took a breath and said, "I hear you. The clothes got wet and that's annoying." Gopika kept shouting. He did not raise his voice. "Can we sort this out tomorrow morning, just the two of us, without everyone watching? I'll bring a drip tray."
Gopika said, "Fine, ten o'clock," and went inside.
I told Tanvir that if it flared up again, the society committee could mediate, and I would note today's events. He thanked me and went up. Will check on both at ten tomorrow.

qa.a: Water dripping from Tanvir's balcony plants onto her washing.

qa.q: What do Tanvir's fists closing and opening suggest?
qa.a: They suggest he felt his own anger rising, then chose to calm himself rather than shout back.

qa.q: How did Tanvir keep the argument from growing?
qa.a: He listened, named Gopika's complaint, stayed quiet in tone, offered a drip tray, and moved the talk to the next morning without an audience.

qa.q: How might Gopika see Tanvir's calm reply?
qa.a: Gopika may feel heard and a little deflated, since there is no one shouting back, which makes agreeing to ten o'clock easier.

grounding: A neighbour shouts at the protagonist over a small matter; he controls his temper, listens, moves the talk away from an audience, and knows the committee can help.

passage:
Jyoti's diary, Tuesday night.
Mr Imran from downstairs banged on my door at 7 today, shouting that my bathroom is leaking into his kitchen ceiling. In front of the whole corridor. The Sharma kids actually came out to watch.
I could feel it climbing in my chest, that urge to shout back "It's not my pipe, it's the building's!" Instead I stepped out and pulled the door almost shut behind me, so it was just us. I said, "I can see you're upset. Let me look tonight and we'll check your ceiling together tomorrow, when the plumber's here." He was still going, but quieter.
After he left I sat on the floor for ten minutes, shaking a bit. Then I texted the plumber and the society secretary, just so there's a record if this gets worse.
Proud of myself, honestly. Still annoyed.

qa.q: What did Mr Imran say was leaking into his kitchen ceiling?
How did Jyoti feel during and after the shouting?
qa.a: Jyoti felt anger climbing in the chest, then was left shaky but proud afterwards, and still annoyed.

qa.q: Which steps helped Jyoti handle the confrontation?
qa.a: Stepping out and pulling the door shut to avoid an audience, acknowledging his upset, offering to check the ceiling tomorrow with the plumber, and texting the society secretary for a record.

qa.q: How might Mr Imran feel after Jyoti's reply?
qa.a: He is probably still worried about his ceiling, but feeling heard makes him quieter and more willing to wait for tomorrow.

grounding: A neighbour shouts over a small matter; the protagonist stays calm, listens, offers to resolve it later away from onlookers, and notes the committee for escalation.
